input.generation: on-the-fly; no input array is allocated

partition: OpenMP schedule(static); each worker owns one local partial state; final state merge occurs in ascending worker index order

measurements.process_cpu_time: CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID nanoseconds, including CPU consumed by all process threads
measurements.speedup: matching serial method median wall time divided by OpenMP method median wall time
measurements.memory: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss process-wide high-water mark ; not a per-method allocation measurement

acceptance.actual_openmp_threads: must equal requested worker count for every repetition
acceptance.serial_naive: expected to fail exact sum for both cancellation layouts

limitations: Synthetic cancellation data is not representative of all scientific workloads.
The generated-on-the-fly input removes input-array memory bandwidth from the benchmark.
Process-wide peak RSS cannot attribute memory to an individual method.
A single hosted runner is not an independent hardware replication.
No wall-time speedup is assumed; thread startup, scheduling and runtime overhead may dominate.
The OpenMP benchmark is Linux/POSIX-oriented because it uses CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID and getrusage.
